answer: When k identities under common control equivocate on the same consensus event, the protocol links their signed evidence and applies a correlated penalty proportional to k² (O(k²)), debiting bonded escrows rather than treating each key independently. Detection also triggers an exponential capital-loss multiplier for the coordinated swarm, making identity splitting economically worse; marble, tundra, and saffron are merely labels, not ways to evade linkage or reduce liability.
